steps.name: Treated vs control composition test
caveats: Deconvolution scores from xCell and MCP-counter are not proportions; a difference in score is a between-sample relative statement about that one cell type only

If the curated marker resource is absent at run time, fall back to a literature-standard marker list written inline in the script and say explicitly in the output which source was used.

grounding.reason: Per-sample signature scores with a rank-based, depth-robust method (R-0133), marker sets from a curated human resource with species and tissue stated (R-0135), and limma on the scores with BH across signatures plus full signature provenance (R-0134). A provenance table: signature name, source, version, number of genes in the definition, number present in the matrix

Explicit statement that the scores are relative enrichments and not cell fractions

steps.context: This step writes no new inference; it consolidates T2S1, T2S2 and T2S3 into the deliverable and records provenance.
steps.question: What is the consolidated per-sample immune and stromal composition of the 12 melanoma biopsies, which differences between anti-PD-1 treated and control survive cross-method agreement, and under what caveats?

plan.title: Melanoma TPM immune/stromal deconvolution: anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The core delivered a gene-level Salmon TPM table only (12,000 gene symbols x 12 melanoma biopsies) plus a 12x2 metadata table with a single condition column (anti-PD-1 treated, n=6, vs untreated control, n=6; unpaired, single batch). The question is compositional — what immune and stromal populations are present in each biopsy, and does composition differ between the arms — so the plan is a deconvolution plan, not a differential-expression plan.

TPM is the correct and expected input scale for the reference-based deconvolution methods (EPIC, quanTIseq), so the absence of raw counts is not limiting for the central question; it only rules out count-based models, which this question does not need. Step T1S1 does sample-structure QC on log2(TPM+1) with PCA, a sample-distance heatmap and detected-gene counts, and explicitly carries sample_01 — profiled at roughly a quarter of the median depth — through the QC rather than dropping it, reporting where it falls on the PCA and how many genes it detects. This matters more than usual here: a shallow library loses low-expressed marker genes first, which biases deconvolution toward the abundant compartments, so sample_01 gets a stated sensitivity check downstream rather than silent inclusion. T1S2 applies the 1-TPM-in-at-least-6-samples floor and produces the log2(TPM+1) matrix; the linear TPM matrix is preserved unfiltered for the deconvolution methods, which expect a full linear-scale profile.

T2S1 is the core step: run quanTIseq and EPIC (absolute fractions with an uncharacterized fraction), MCP-counter (between-sample abundance scores), xCell (64-type enrichment scores) and ConsensusTME through the single immunedeconv interface on linear TPM, and report every method side by side per sample. No single method ranks first for every cell type, so a composition claim requires agreement in direction between two or more methods. CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE are license-restricted and absent from this environment, so no LM22 result and no tumour-purity number will be claimed; the EPIC/quanTIseq uncharacterized fraction and the xCell immune/stroma scores are reported as relative stand-ins with that stated. T2S2 tests the treated-vs-control difference per cell type with limma on the fraction/score matrix (reference level = control, contrast treated - control), BH-adjusted across cell types within each method, and reports effect sizes with confidence intervals. With 6 vs 6 this is underpowered for anything but large compositional shifts, and the step must say so rather than report a null as evidence of no difference.

T2S3 is an orthogonal, marker-based read of the same question: UCell rank-based per-sample scores for immune and stromal cell-type marker sets and for IO-relevant signatures (cytotoxic/CD8 effector, IFN-gamma, exhaustion, checkpoint genes including PDCD1/CD274/CTLA4/LAG3, TGF-beta/fibroblast stroma), tested with the same design and BH-adjusted across signatures. Rank-based scoring is depth-robust, which is exactly the property needed given sample_01. These scores are enrichments, not fractions, and are reported as such. T2S4 collects everything into one per-sample composition table plus the reproducibility record.

What this plan deliberately does not do: it does not run gene-level differential expression or enrichment, because the research question asks for composition and a DE run would be unasked scope; and it does not claim tumour purity. Method choices, filters and the low-depth policy are grounded in the returned procedure (snapshot sha256:90c6875...).

quanTIseq, EPIC, MCP-counter, xCell and ConsensusTME via immunedeconv on linear TPM, consensus across methods

limma on cell-type fractions/scores with BH across cell types
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seed, package and signature versions

steps.name: Treated vs control composition test
steps.question: Does any immune or stromal cell type differ in estimated abundance between the 6 anti-PD-1 treated and the 6 untreated control melanoma biopsies, consistently across methods?
steps.description: Test the treated-vs-control difference for every cell type in the T2S1 output. Fit limma on the cell-type score matrix per method with design ~condition, reference level set explicitly to control so a positive coefficient means higher in treated; use eBayes with robust=TRUE and trend=TRUE. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg across cell types WITHIN each method. Report per cell type: the estimate with a 95% confidence interval, the raw and adjusted p-value, and the direction, for each method side by side. Mark a cell type as a robust compositional difference only when two or more methods agree on the direction and at least one reaches BH-adjusted p < 0.05; report everything else as not robust. Add a leave-sample_01-out re-run of the same test as a sensitivity check and report whether any call changes.
steps.context: 6 vs 6 unpaired, single batch, one condition factor — this design detects only large compositional shifts. Deconvolution scores carry their own estimation error on top of biological variance, which widens the effective noise further. The honest output is a ranked table with effect sizes and intervals, not a significance verdict.

Reference level and contrast stated explicitly as condition, numerator treated, denominator control
BH adjustment applied across cell types within each method, with the number of cell types tested reported
A consensus column marking cell types where two or more methods agree in direction
Leave-sample_01-out sensitivity re-run reported, stating whether any consensus call changes
An explicit written statement that with n=6 per group the analysis is underpowered for small and moderate compositional shifts and that a non-significant result is not evidence of no difference
constraints: Set the reference level of condition to control explicitly; do not rely on alphabetical ordering
limma with eBayes(robust=TRUE, trend=TRUE) on the score matrix; a Wilcoxon rank-sum test may be reported beside it as a distribution-free check
BH across cell types within each method; report the count of tests
Do not fit a count-based model (DESeq2/edgeR/voom) — the input is TPM-derived scores, not counts
Do not select results by unadjusted p-value or by effect size alone
Cell-type estimates are the OUTCOME here, not a covariate; state that role in the report
caveats: Deconvolution scores from xCell and MCP-counter are not proportions; a difference in score is a between-sample relative statement about that one cell type only

Compositional estimates from absolute-fraction methods are constrained to sum with the uncharacterized fraction, so an apparent increase in one type can reflect a decrease elsewhere — state this when interpreting
n=6 vs 6 with method-level estimation error: confidence intervals will be wide

grounding.reason: Composition compared between groups: limma on the per-sample scores under the study design with BH across cell types (R-0134, R-0044) and robust/trend moderation (R-0093), explicit reference level (R-0036), a claim only where two or more methods agree (R-0128), and the estimate stated as the outcome (R-0132).

steps.name: Marker-based immune and IO signature scoring
steps.question: Do rank-based immune, stromal and immuno-oncology signature scores per sample corroborate the deconvolution result, and do they differ between anti-PD-1 treated and control biopsies?
steps.description: Compute UCell rank-based per-sample scores on the filtered log2(TPM+1) matrix for (a) immune and stromal cell-type marker sets — CD8 T, CD4 T, Treg, NK, B/plasma, monocyte/macrophage, dendritic, neutrophil, mast, endothelial, fibroblast/CAF — and (b) IO-relevant signatures: cytotoxic/CD8 effector, IFN-gamma response, T-cell exhaustion, checkpoint genes (PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4, LAG3, HAVCR2, TIGIT), and a TGF-beta/stromal set. Take the cell-type markers from a curated marker resource for human immune and tumour-microenvironment cell types available in the environment (for example the human tumour-microenvironment gating marker table in the reference store), and take the pathway-level sets from a human pathway collection in the reference store. Record for every signature its source, its version and the number of its genes present in this 12,000-gene matrix. Test each score for the treated - control contrast with limma under the same design as T2S2 (reference level control), BH-adjusted across signatures. Report scores per sample as a heatmap alongside the deconvolution fractions.
steps.context: Rank-based scoring is robust to sequencing depth because ranks are computed within a sample, which makes it the right orthogonal check given sample_01's low depth. These are enrichment scores, not fractions. The 12,000-gene matrix is a subset of the transcriptome, so some signature genes will be missing — the count of present genes must be reported per signature because a signature missing genes is a different signature. If the curated marker resource is absent at run time, fall back to a literature-standard marker list written inline in the script and say explicitly in the output which source was used.

A provenance table: signature name, source, version, number of genes in the definition, number present in the matrix
limma test of each score for treated - control with BH across signatures, reporting estimate, CI, p and adjusted p
Explicit statement that the scores are relative enrichments and not cell fractions

The marker source actually used is named in the output, including whether a fallback inline list was used
constraints: Score on log2(TPM+1) values with a rank-based per-sample method (UCell); singscore is an acceptable alternative for a signature with an up and a down set
Markers must be HUMAN and appropriate to tumour/skin tissue; state the species and tissue of origin of the marker sets
Test the scores with limma under the study design; BH across signatures; state the number of signatures tested
Report the number of signature genes present in the matrix for every signature
Do not present an enrichment score as a proportion
caveats: A marker of a cell type in one tissue is not necessarily a marker of that type in another tissue

The delivered matrix holds 12,000 genes, not the full transcriptome, so signatures will be partially covered — coverage must be reported, and a signature with very low coverage should be flagged rather than scored silently
